I'm 68 this year, been farming this land for 45 years. My family has 13.1 mu of flat land in Quzhou. My son and daughter-in-law work in a factory over in Handan, so mostly it's me and my wife in the fields, though they come back for harvest. I only finished primary school, but I know this soil better than any book.

I always plant winter wheat right after National Day, around October 5th to 10th, once the weather cools down. I buy the same improved wheat seed from the county seed station — costs me about 30 yuan per mu. I don't chase fancy new varieties. My neighbor Old Wang tried some new seed last year and it didn't do any better than mine, so why pay more?

For fertilizer, I'm careful because cash is tight. Before planting wheat, I spread half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu as my base — that's about 25 kilos. Then in spring, when the wheat starts jointing and if it looks a little yellow, I topdress with another half bag of urea per mu, about 20 kilos. That's what I've done for years. My nephew says I should use more, but he farms over 100 mu and has more money to spend. I'd rather not risk running short of cash for my wife's medicine.

I irrigate the wheat three times: once right after planting if the soil is dry, once at green-up around March, and once at grain filling in May. Pumping water from the well costs electricity, so I don't waste it. Three times is enough if you watch the sky. Old Wang does four, but I think that's spending money for nothing.

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June — around June 8th or 10th — I get the summer maize in the ground. The window is tight, maybe five or six days, so I hire a tractor with a planter. I can't do that by hand at my age, and there's no time. I plant hybrid maize seed, about 50 yuan per mu. I put down a bit more than half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then topdress with half a bag of urea when the maize is knee-high. I irrigate twice for maize if the rains don't come — once at planting and once at tasseling. If the summer is wet, maybe only once.

For pests, I spray herbicide on both crops. Sometimes aphids hit the wheat in spring, then I use insecticide. For maize, if I see corn borers, I treat it. I do the spraying myself with my backpack sprayer — hiring someone for that is a waste.

Most of the work is me and my wife. We hire two days of help for wheat harvest and two days for maize harvest — young men from the village, we pay them 100 yuan a day and give them lunch. Family labor is precious because my wife also has to manage the house, and I can't bend and lift like I did at forty.

I expect about 400 kilos per mu for wheat, and maybe 450 for maize if the summer rains are good. Last year wheat was 380 and maize was 420. I'm not greedy — I just need enough to feed us and sell a bit for cash. Total spending this year, I figure around 6,000 yuan. That's a lot for us, but you have to spend to eat. I stick with what I know because change is risky when you're my age.
